rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-judged after the AI/model→agent/LLM word-swap diff (8651e524..HEAD, lines 17,23,47,55,63). Chunk 0 line 17 'the agent's raw power' is the file's first use of 'agent' — checked with `grep -n -iE '\bagent' ` (all hits printed in this session): no in-file antecedent precedes it, but 'agent' is AE101's own spine noun (the training is literally Agentic Engineering) established long before this supplementary page in the module arc — arc-earned spine vocabulary carve-out, not a coined referent needing binding. Chunk 2 (line 47) now reads 'agent's search space… asking the LLM to infer… the agent has a concrete signal… the agent has more room to improvise' — 'LLM' and 'agent' name the same underlying system under the split `curriculum/vocabulary.md` line 48 already prescribes ('thinking → the LLM; acting → the agent'): 'infer' is the thinking verb (correctly LLM), 'has a concrete signal' / 'has more room to improvise' are acting-register (correctly agent) — the pronoun 'it' in 'gives it many small, local tripwires' binds to the nearest antecedent 'the LLM'. Not ambiguous, just two controlled terms doing their controlled jobs. Chunks 4 and 6 each re-use 'agent(s)'/'agentic' already named earlier in the SAME chunk before switching to 'an agent' (chunk 4 line 55: 'agents can generate…' then 'an agent to satisfy'; chunk 6 line 63: 'the agentic reason' then 'An agent operating…' twice) — clean in-chunk antecedents. Chunk 5's CRAP-gloss pronoun question is the maintainer's own accept-note (line 109): 'Both' at line 59 binds to 'CRAP' + 'complexity metrics' both named in the same bolded lead — scored PASS per that note, no pronoun proposed. Checked every other demonstrative in the body (line 15 'That alone', line 19 'This is the mercury problem', line 21, line 23 'this is where', line 63 'This is classic Clean Code', line 67 'it needs instruments', line 73 'a clue', line 105 'the steering system') — each resolves against the immediately preceding sentence inside its own chunk. Harm (an unresolvable referent stalling a reader) absent everywhere.

No callback to another curriculum file by position anywhere in body; all links are external X citations, named by platform ('Uncle Bob, [X](url)'), not located by page position. Diff touched only single-word swaps inside sentences, none link-adjacent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Standalone supplementary reading, not an exercise/lecture inside a module arc; no 'the X you did/saw' beat references anywhere in body, before or after the diff.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal structure anywhere in the file; expository practitioner-synthesis prose only. The diff's word-swaps sit inside declarative sentences, not a demo beat.

Every ## chunk (1-9) carries a self-contained claim about one named practice plus at least one supporting quote or elaboration; none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet. Unaffected by the diff (word-level swaps only, no structural change).

Chunk 2 header 'Unit tests shrink the agent's room to improvise' (line 45) now matches its own closing sentence even more tightly post-diff: 'When the tests are absent, vague, or too broad, the agent has more room to improvise' (line 47) — 'agent' replacing 'model' pulls the body noun into alignment with the header's own noun. Chunk 9 header 'A prompt biases the agent, it does not bind it' (line 93) vs body 'Natural language is not enough… tests, tools, structure, metrics, and feedback loops' (line 95) is a synthesis of that sentence plus the Dijkstra quote rather than verbatim, but stays inside, unaffected by the diff. All other headers (Acceptance tests / TDD / Mutation testing / Metrics / Small units / Architecture / Human's job) restate their chunk's opening bolded-lead sentence near-verbatim, none touched by the word-swap diff.

Ran fresh greps this session over body (lines 1-106): `grep -n -E '\. Not [A-Za-z]+\.'` → 0 hits (no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.'); `grep -n -iE 'one of the most|most useful|best way|game-chang|revolution'` → 0 hits (no self-grading superlative); `grep -n -iE 'could be (more|less)|roughly|approximately'` → 0 hits (no number+retraction shape). Closest anaphora-triple candidate is the verbatim, oEmbed-verified Uncle Bob quote at lines 85-91 ('Assemblers were faster… Compilers were faster… AIs are faster… Deal with it.') — an attributed direct quote (source stamp martin-ais-are-faster), not authored cadence, so altering it to satisfy this rule would falsify sourced text; reported as a rule question, not filed REVISE, consistent with the prior instance. No abstraction-noun stacks or empty-leg verb triplets found. None of the diff's five word-swaps (AI/model → agent/LLM) touches this rule's shapes.

'LLM' (line 47, new post-diff) is not repo-internal dialect — it is standard industry vocabulary and is one of the three controlled terms `curriculum/vocabulary.md` line 48 explicitly names for student-facing body use ('LLM / the agent / Claude'). Chunk 0 and chunk 9 carry zero bold. The diff's word-swaps all landed in unbolded body sentences (lines 17, 23, 47, 55, 63) — bold inventory unchanged from prior instance.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read `site/layouts/slides.js` lines 229-262 this session (not carried forward from a prior claim): in the composed whole-handbook deck, `buildDeckModel` walks `root.querySelectorAll(':scope > section.module')` — the comment at line 237 states explicitly 'A prose section with no phases — prework, supplementary, reference — is slide-ified in place under a kind-labelled divider,' i.e. supplementary pages get a top-level `section.module` wrapper and reach the deck. When this file is opened standalone (`!phases.length` branch, line 229-232), `buildSingleDoc(root, …)` renders it directly with no phase filtering. Either path reaches the deck; the diff only changed body words, not the file's section/heading structure, so presence is unaffected by this edit.
